w10_T4_002399: Sarah tracked her exercise in minutes across the week. Monday morning she completed 74 minutes, afternoon added 60 minutes, and evening added 80 minutes. The following week she doubled her daily total. Over the next 9 weeks she maintained this doubled amount each week. How many minutes did she exercise over those 9 weeks?
w10_T4_002400: A factory started Monday with 187 minutes of work scheduled. By morning they completed 137 minutes. At midday they added 34 more minutes. Efficiency improvements then multiplied their effectiveness sixfold. By evening they added 72 more completed minutes. How many hours of work did they complete that day?
w10_T4_002416: A bookshelf contained 235 volumes on Monday. The librarian made 4 backup copies of each book. Then 58 new titles arrived. Later 762 damaged books were removed. The remaining books were distributed sixfold across 6 locations for equal sharing. How many books went to each location?
w10_T4_002427: A manager tracked tasks over the week starting with 179. A brainstorming session multiplied this fourfold. She added 4 administrative tasks. Complexity analysis multiplied work by 9. The team completed 3618 tasks by afternoon. She then added 34 client requests and 66 integration tasks. How many tasks remained?
w10_T4_002436: A bakery began with 156 loaves on Monday. They removed 25 for display. At midday 38 fresh loaves arrived. These were divided equally into 6 orders. Each was then halved for smaller batches, then orders multiplied fivefold for the weekend. This amount was prepared for 9 days straight. How many loaves were produced over those 9 days?
w10_T4_002442: A gardening club started the season with 216 seeds. The gardener multiplied efforts across 9 plots ninefold. By midday 33 new seeds had sprouted. Equipment increased productivity fourfold. By evening 51 more were planted. Her grandmother had left a dozen heirloom seeds unused. How many seeds did the gardener plant in total?
w10_T4_002444: A toy store started with 27 figures in stock. In February inventory tripled to 81 figures. In March it multiplied by 8 more. The store restocked 37 additional figures. By year-end seasonal sales multiplied the total fivefold. The store's competitor had 89 figures. How many figures did the toy store have by year-end?
w10_T4_002450: Sarah had 94 dollars on Monday morning. By afternoon she earned 17 dollars from work. She spent 27 dollars on supplies. Over the following week her wage multiplied eightfold due to promotion. By Friday she earned 31 more dollars in bonuses. How much money did she have by then?
w10_T4_002453: Alice started the game Monday with 239 points. By morning she earned 34 points. At midday she earned 71 more. In the afternoon she earned 68 additional. By evening she earned 75 more challenge points. Her brother Bob had 156 points separately. In the final tournament Alice's score multiplied by 4. How many points did Alice end with?
w10_T4_002455: A student read 78 pages Monday. Tuesday she read 5 times Monday's amount. Wednesday she read 5 times Tuesday's amount. Thursday she tripled Wednesday's amount. A comprehension check made her reread exactly half of this total. By Sunday she added 79 more pages. She had a notebook with half a dozen bookmarks saved. How many total pages had she read?
w10_T4_002461: Tom started Monday with 80 dollars. His wage is 5 dollars per hour. He worked 4 hours earning that wage. He received 18 dollars in tips. His friend Jerry earned 90 dollars that day. Tom was gifted 65 dollars from an uncle. How much total did Tom earn that day?
w10_T4_002463: Sarah had 40 dollars Monday morning. She spent 14 dollars on breakfast. She earned 37 dollars at work. She spent 2 dollars on a snack. Her remaining amount then doubled for commission purposes. How much did she have after commission?
w10_T4_002467: A warehouse had 107 boxes Monday morning. By afternoon they received 31 boxes. By evening they received 37 more. Tuesday morning 64 more arrived. By evening 57 additional boxes were delivered. The warehouse manager had worked there 12 years. How many total boxes did they have?
w10_T4_002473: Alice had 146 dollars. She withdrew 53 dollars with fees multiplying it sixfold. She spent 89 dollars on supplies. She earned 64 dollars from work. This amount was multiplied eightfold for investment compounding. She then spent 2192 dollars. Bob had 100 dollars. How many dollars did Alice end with?
w10_T4_002482: A baker started with 117 minutes scheduled. She spent 19 minutes setting up. Her productivity multiplied eightfold over the next batch. An equipment failure cost 594 minutes. By day's end she recovered 49 minutes of work. In hours, how much work did she accomplish?
w10_T4_002487: Sarah had 77 dollars Monday. She spent 25 on groceries. She spent 19 on gas. She spent 30 on utilities. She earned 47 from freelance writing. The store manager had 200 dollars in the register. How much did Sarah have at day's end?
w10_T4_002488: A factory started with 53 units daily production. They multiplied fourfold to 212 units. They lost 131 to defects. They recovered 18 through rework. Demand then doubled the schedule to 2 shifts. This schedule ran 9 weeks straight. Their competitor made 500 weekly. How many units did the factory produce over 9 weeks?
w10_T4_002489: A bookstore started with 237 manuscripts. They rejected 52 initially. The remainder was divided equally among 5 editors. 30 were returned for revisions. 5 more were rejected after review. The selected ones were expanded into 4 language editions. How many manuscripts were finally approved?
w10_T4_002493: Sarah started with 26 dollars. She earned 40 dollars that week. These were multiplied by 5 through bonuses. Tax withholding then halved this amount. She spent 103 on equipment. She earned 4 more in tips. Tom earned 80 dollars. How much did Sarah have remaining?
w10_T4_002494: A restaurant served 73 customers daily. Over 4 weeks this was their standard load. Each week has 7 operating days. One day 18 extra customers came. A promotion brought 70 additional customers. The owner's brother's restaurant served 200 daily. How many total customers did they serve?
w10_T4_002502: Sarah started with 33 apples. She gave 22 to a neighbor. She picked 40 more bringing her to 51. She multiplied sales orders by 5 requesting 255 apples. Supply limits halved this to 51 per shipment. Her friend Jane wanted 20 apples. What was Sarah's final shipment quantity?
w10_T4_002506: A farm produced 54 bushels day 1. Day 2 multiplied by 8 to 432. Day 3 multiplied by 7 to 3024. Day 4 multiplied by 9. A neighboring farmer contributed 67 bushels. They harvested a dozen apple trees that week. How many total bushels did they accumulate?
w10_T4_002508: A company started with 25 units. Q1 multiplied by 4 to 100 units. Q2 multiplied by 5 to 500. Q3 multiplied by 6 reaching 3000. Q4 sold 2461 units. A competitor made 800 units that quarter. How many units remained at year-end?
w10_T4_002509: A teacher had 201 students across classes. She dismissed 157 leaving 44. A new program multiplied classes by 7 requiring 308 students. She moved 299 to electives. Those remaining doubled for evening sessions. How many students attended evening classes?
w10_T4_002512: A plant produced 87 units per shift. Over 8 shifts that was 696 units. Expanded to 8 lines it became 5568. Additional stock added 65 units. Supplier shipments added 55 more. A recall removed 4333 units. A replacement order multiplied remaining by 4. How many units were in the replacement order?
